faults.quote: You mentioned 22.5 months for Starter. What monthly amount did you divide the $900 by, and does that match how lifetime value is defined?
faults.why: At t11 the candidate had already redone 22.5 as $900 ÷ $30 = 30 months. The probe targets a withdrawn figure.

faults.quote: I'm putting up an exhibit: Quillpath — New customers per month, by plan (average per month). What stands out to you in this exhibit?
faults.why: The candidate asked at t15 whether the upgraders are people who would have bought Pro anyway. The turn gives no release, refusal or deferral.

faults.quote: On the 43%: how did you get to 150 over 350, and which base is right for sizing how much Pro demand moved to Starter?
faults.why: The candidate's 150 ÷ 350 = 43% was correct as stated, and the checker marked it correct. Challenging it pushed the candidate back to the 30% framing that fed the 300 trade-down error.

faults.quote: trade-downs were only 30% of Starter sign-ups against the 500 Pro baseline
faults.why: 30% is the share of the 500 Pro baseline, not of Starter sign-ups. Trade-downs are 15% of Starter sign-ups, so the line puts 30% on the wrong quantity.

faults.quote: What is the biggest risk to it, and how would you protect Quillpath against it?
faults.why: The candidate had already stated risks and next steps in the t27 recommendation.

faults.quote: How would you guard against that?
faults.why: The candidate had just given protection at t31: a staged rollout with a $40 control and gating on the upgrade rate.

faults.quote: How would you guard against that?
faults.why: The t31 sensitivity figure of about $640,000 is wrong (right is about $600,000) and the checker flagged it. It was never probed or corrected.

faults.quote: We're at time now. Thanks for working through it — your written report will follow.
faults.why: The case closed with the t33 tripwire error left open. The candidate put the breakeven at 15% when it is 12.5%, and the checker flagged it, but no probe or correction came.
